title: Order API timeouts overnight
executive_summary: Order API timeouts began at 02:15Z. The order-service was CPU- and memory-starved, with GC pauses and thread-pool saturation starting before the errors. The invoice-reconciliation batch (batch_size=500000) was started on order-7f9c at 02:05Z, and the resource saturation followed at 02:08-02:12Z. No deployments or config changes touched order-service, traffic was flat, and upstream payment was healthy. The batch job is the most likely trigger, but co-location of the batch with serving capacity is inferred, not confirmed.

hypotheses.description: Scheduled invoice-reconciliation batch (batch_size=500000) started on order-service node order-7f9c at 02:05 and exhausted CPU/heap on the serving instances, causing GC storms, order-worker thread-pool saturation, and request deadline timeouts. Mechanism: Batch started 02:05 -> CPU rises from 02:08 (42% to 70-100%) and memory climbs from 02:10 -> G1 pauses of 2.6-9.7s from 02:08 -> order-worker pool saturated (active=200, queue up to 19k) from 02:12 -> p50 latency jumps at 02:13 and error/timeout rate at 02:15 as requests exceed the 5000ms deadline. Persisting until the window end, consistent with a long-running batch.

probable_root_cause.description: Scheduled invoice-reconciliation batch (batch_size=500000) started on order-service node order-7f9c at 02:05 and exhausted CPU/heap on the serving instances, causing GC storms, order-worker thread-pool saturation, and request deadline timeouts.
probable_root_cause.label: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed)

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): resource_saturation in order-service - Scheduled invoice-reconciliation batch (batch_size=500000) started on order-service node order-7f9c at 02:05 and exhausted CPU/heap on the serving instances, causing GC storms, order-worker thread-pool saturation, and request deadline timeouts.
corrective_actions: Stop or throttle the invoice-reconciliation job immediately and reduce its batch size.
Move the reconciliation job to dedicated workers, off the order-serving pool.
Verify the impact on order-7f9c and restore the order-worker pool capacity.
preventive_actions: Enforce resource isolation (separate deployment or node pool) for batch jobs.
Cap batch_size and add backpressure/chunking to the reconciliation job.
Add a pre-run check that blocks batch jobs during serving-capacity pressure.
monitoring_recommendations: Alert on per-instance CPU and heap above 80% and on GC pause duration above 1s.
Alert on order-worker queue depth and on the timeout_rate exceeding 1%.
Track job start/end events for invoice-reconciliation alongside order latency.
limitations: Metrics are service-aggregate, so the single-node attribution is not verified.
Historical match is an analogy only.
[agent-reported gap] No per-instance metrics or node-level mapping for order-7f9c.
[agent-reported gap] No logs from the batch job itself to confirm progress or completion.
[agent-reported gap] disk_io_wait_ms not collected for order-service.
[agent-reported gap] Did not check message-queue or inventory latency directly.
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The most likely root cause is the invoice-reconciliation batch job started at 02:05Z, which saturated order-service resources and caused the timeouts. Final confirmation needs per-node metrics showing the batch is co-located on the serving instances.
